**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted).
• Construction zones: 35 mph unless otherwise posted. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “seat‑belt law” for teens; however, Texas has a “no‑seat‑belt” law for 16‑year‑olds who are not yet licensed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield” signs give priority to the vehicle already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.003 | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop sign.
• Vehicles must stop on both sides of the road. | Texas Transportation Code §545.004 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other vehicles.
• “No‑passing” zones on two‑lane roads. | Texas Transportation Code §545.005 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a “no parking” zone is a ticket. | Texas Transportation Code §545.006 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only when the vehicle is unsafe or obstructing traffic.
• Towing a vehicle without a permit can result in a fine. | Texas Transportation Code §545.007 | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights and sirens. | Texas Transportation Code §545.008 | | **Roadside Assistance & Breakdown** | • Pull over to the shoulder, turn on hazard lights, and call 911 if you need help. | Texas Transportation Code §545.009 | --- ### How to Get the Full Legal Text 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The official source for all traffic laws. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TS/htm/TS.545.htm 2. **TxDOT – Traffic Safety** – Offers summaries, statistics, and educational materials. *Website:* https://www.txdot.gov/inside-txdot/traffic-safety.html 3. **TxDMV – Driver Handbook** – Practical guide for drivers, including licensing and registration. *Website:* https://www.txdmv.gov/handbooks --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for safety. - **Keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – no texting or handheld phone use. - **Check for school buses** – stop even if you’re not in the same lane. - **Use turn signals** – they’re required by law and help prevent accidents. - **Stay alert for construction zones** – speed limits may drop to 35 mph. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
